sentences.text: Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellants and respondents.
The ranks of the parties are retained as per tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. Brief facts of the case is that one G. Chandra Shekar met with an accident on 16.05.2022 and died subsequently.
His parents filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.
The Tribunal considering the entire evidence on record granted an amount of Rs.22,62,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% from date of petition till realisation.

sentences.text: Tribunal assessed the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner as 40% and that of the driver of the offending vehicle as 60%.
Accordingly, directed to deposit Rs.13,57,440 with interest at the rate of 7% p.a. from date of petition till realisation.

Aggrieved by the said order this appeal is preferred in which it is mainly contented that Chandrasekhar was working as a supervisor in G-Mart and also owning his own cab and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.

But the Tribunal has NC:
2026:KHC:6913 HC-KAR considered only Rs.15,500/- per month without any basis and granted meager compensation and interest is to be granted at the rate of 12% instead of 6%.
5.
Though it is stated that Chandrasekhar was earning Rs.50,000/- per month, claimants have not filed any income proof.
As he met with an accident in the year 2022 the tribunal rightly considered his notional income as Rs.15,500/- per month.
He was aged 28 years and the multiplier taken is 17.
The petitioner is entitled for 40% towards future prospects and as he is a bachelor 50% is to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Loss of dependency comes to Rs.15,500 + 40% x 12 x 17 - 50% = Rs.22,13,400/-
The claimants are parents of the deceased and each of them are entitled for an amount of Rs.44,000/- towards filial consortium and also Rs.33,000/- under the conventional head.
6. Thus in all, components awarded by this court are as below, NC: 2026:KHC:6913 HC-KAR Amount Sl.Nos.

Particulars in Rs.
 1 Towards loss of dependency 22,13,400  2 Towards loss of consortium 88,000  (2 claimants)
 3 Conventional heads 33,000

Hence, the compensation granted by tribunal is enhanced from Rs.22,62,400/- to Rs.23,34,400/-
along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
7.
Further, learned counsel for appellant stated that Tribunal erred in fixing 40% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased and it is to be modified.

The manner of accident shows on 16.05.2022 while he was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39/CG-5128 along with two pillion riders on the outer ring road of Karthiknagar Service Road, near Karnataka Bank, Bengaluru,
at that time a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL- 05/AT-7732 came in a rash and negligent manner and NC: 2026:KHC:6913 HC-KAR dashed this motorcycle.
As a result, he fell down and died on the spot.

It was observed by the Tribunal that G.Chandra Shekar and other pillion riders were not wearing any helmet and it is a triple riding and charge sheet is filed against the riders of both the motor vehicles and accordingly assessed the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased as 40%.
If it is a case of triple riding with no helmet, fine will be imposed.
But charge sheet is filed against the riders of both the vehicles on the ground that it is a head-on collusion.

Hence, the compensation granted by tribunal is enhanced from Rs.10,76,360/- to Rs.12,87,800/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
15.

ORDER i.
Appeal is allowed in part.
